summary: I used to think wildfire fuel reduction was mostly about removing big wood. The more I read, the more it looks like a question of vertical structure: a stand with a clean gap under the crowns can burn mildly even with a lot of biomass, while continuous low vegetation lets a ground fire climb. By studying years of sea surface temperature measurements from satellites, the authors found that weak SSTGs preceded a storm’s rapid intensification.
